name: Apothecary
description: A precise poisoner-healer who uses a silent blowpipe, weapon poisons, and salves. Supports the party with field medicine and clever alchemical prep.
suggestedSkills: Archery, Crafting, Nature, Lore, Perception, Insight, Education

recommendedTalents.name: Disciplined Archer
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re-roll one ranged attack per scene

recommendedTalents.name: Peak Performance
recommendedTalents.gloss: Pre‑buff one weapon or ammo: +1 weapon damage or +2 ammo damage until next rest

recommendedTalents.name: Poison Maker
recommendedTalents.gloss: Brew your own poisons in the field, up to Quality 2

recommendedCombatArts.name: Aimed Shot
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain +1 boon when you don’t move

recommendedCombatArts.name: Precise Shot
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Ignore armor and add Agility to damage

startingEquipment.note: one use spent per poison you brew
replaces your standard pack: no load of its own, +2 carrying capacity

playstyle: The Apothecary rewards patience, setup, and smart resource use. Open from stealth with the silent blowpipe. Coat darts with Weapon Poison and use the blowpipe property to multiply the poison’s damage on strong/critical hits. Peak Performance lets you boost your darts (ammo) for +2 damage the whole day, turning small hits into meaningful chip. Poison Maker lets you brew your own weapon poisons in the field, so your damage never depends on what you could afford to buy: spend an exploration turn, one use of materials, and roll Spirit or Mind + Nature. Use Aimed Shot to land reliable first strikes and Precise Shot to punch through armor when needed.
advancement: Raise Archery 2-3 for more Combat Arts and consistency (Sharpshooter or Rapid Shot next). Push Nature 2-3 for higher-Quality poisons and a second brew per rest (Field Medic next if the party wants a medic), and Crafting 2-3 for stronger prep (Efficient Worker, Artisan, or Peak Performance 2). Add Lore for formula lore and Education for scholarly support. Consider Stealth later to exploit blowpipe ambushes with Assassination synergy.

name: Bard
description: A social performer who channels magic through music and story, inspiring allies and shaping encounters with illusions and charm effects.
suggestedSkills: Mysticism, Influence, Education, Survival, Perception, Nature, Stealth

recommendedTalents.name: Master of Principles
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re-roll a mystic rank 0 spell test once per scene

recommendedTalents.name: Inspire Ally
recommendedTalents.gloss: Quick Action: give an ally +1 boon on their next test

recommendedTalents.name: Diplomat
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re-roll Education about a culture‘s values, taboos, or etiquette once per scene

playstyle: The Bard shines in social scenes and soft control. Your rank 0 spells cost no Focus, so they are your every-round tools, and Master of Principles re-rolls one of them each scene. Whispers of Doubt is your answer once blades are drawn: psychic damage that ignores armor, and a confused enemy on a strong hit. Tranquil Mind heals an ally or dazes an enemy from the same casting. Calming Influence shapes tempo before a fight starts, though it suffers +1 bane against anyone already in danger. Inspire Ally fuels allies’ key rolls, while Diplomat means you know what a court, a caravan or a war band expects of you before you open your mouth. You can still carry a shortsword, but your magic and words are your real weapons.
advancement: Raise Mysticism 2-3 to expand spells and reliability (Communal Practices next if you want multi‑target flexibility). Boost Influence 2-3 for stronger team support (Leading Presence is a great pick). Add Education/Lore for cultural/magical knowledge, and optionally Stealth for infiltration and stagecraft. If you want an animal companion, raise Nature to rank 1 and spend its talent on Animal Companion: nothing in your starting build grants one.

name: Barbarian
description: A devastating melee combatant who channels primal fury into brutal attacks, trading defense for raw power.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Athletics, Fortitude, Survival, Perception, Nature, Stealth

recommendedTalents.name: Heavy Weapon Mastery
recommendedTalents.gloss: No bane on Brutal Strike with heavy weapons

recommendedTalents.name: Bulky
recommendedTalents.gloss: +2 HP, and carry more

recommendedTalents.name: Battle Rage
recommendedTalents.gloss: Enter rage for combat bonuses

recommendedCombatArts.name: Brutal Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Deal extra Strength damage with heavy weapons (no bane thanks to Heavy Weapon Mastery!)

recommendedCombatArts.name: Cleave
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Hit multiple enemies with your greataxe

startingEquipment.note: for targets you cannot reach, though you throw it untrained
the only protection your rage still allows

playstyle: The Barbarian is perfect for players who want to deal massive damage and play aggressively, accepting risk for reward. Battle Rage provides combat bonuses while Heavy Weapon Mastery makes Brutal Strike attacks deadly without suffering banes. Bulky gives you extra HP to survive when rage runs out. You wear no armor at all, because rage requires it: a shield or helmet is still allowed, but your greataxe needs both hands. A helmet is the one piece of protection you can still wear, and it is where your coins went: AV 1 from turn one, with your HP doing the rest of the work. Use Cleave to hit multiple foes and Brutal Strike for single-target devastation.
advancement: Raise Fortitude to rank 2 first and take Body of Bronze: unarmored, it gives you 1 + Fortitude as AV, which is the armor your rage forbids you to buy. Then increase Battle Rage for greater power, raise Fighting to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts, add Survival for wilderness expertise, and consider Hard to Kill for surviving what gets through.

name: Brawler
description: A street-tough close-quarters fighter who dominates the clinch with fists, improvised weapons, and dirty tricks.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Fortitude, Streetwise, Influence, Perception, Stealth, Insight

recommendedTalents.name: Dual Wielder
recommendedTalents.gloss: Attack with a weapon in each fist without suffering banes

recommendedTalents.name: Hard to Kill
recommendedTalents.gloss: Shrug off punishment and stay standing in ugly brawls

recommendedTalents.name: Thug Tactics
recommendedTalents.gloss: Gain boons when ganging up or fighting dirty in tight quarters

recommendedCombatArts.name: Disarm
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Knock weapons from enemy hands to tilt the exchange

recommendedCombatArts.name: Head Smack
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Crack them across the skull: they roll Fortitude or end up confused

playstyle: Close distance and take away your opponent’s best options. A cestus in each fist is the whole point: Dual Wielder means you swing both without the banes that punish anyone else for trying. Disarm strips a weapon out of their hands, and Head Smack leaves them confused when the skull rings. Thug Tactics rewards ganging up, so fight where your allies are. You won’t out-damage a greataxe and you aren’t meant to: you take away what the enemy was going to do, and let the party finish it.
advancement: Raise Fighting 2-3 for more control arts (Supreme Disarm) and improved damage lines. Add Fortitude for toughness and recovery, and consider Streetwise 2 for better gang-up play. A spiked chain extends your control footprint once your technique improves, though it costs you the second fist. Pugilist is also open later if you ever want to fight with nothing in your hands at all.

name: Champion
description: A holy warrior combining divine magic with frontline combat, protected by heavy armor and faith.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Mysticism, Influence, Fortitude, Insight, Lore, Perception

recommendedTalents.name: Shield Mastery
recommendedTalents.gloss: Quick Action when hit: reduce the attack‘s Success Level by one step

recommendedTalents.name: Mystic Champion
recommendedTalents.gloss: Infuse a rank 0 mystic spell into a weapon attack

recommendedTalents.name: Leading Presence
recommendedTalents.gloss: Allies near you gain boons to Initiative and vs fear

recommendedCombatArts.name: Defensive Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain Defend Action effects on hit

recommendedCombatArts.name: Terrifying Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Frighten enemies with divine presence

playstyle: The Champion is perfect for players who want to be a holy warrior combining divine magic with frontline tanking. Use Mystic Champion to infuse a rank 0 spell into a melee attack. Shield Mastery is your Quick Action when an enemy connects, dropping their Success Level by a step, and it is what makes you hold a line at AV 1. Leading Presence makes you a natural party leader, and Clear Mind pulls an ally out of a charm or a psychic hit. Use Defensive Strike to stay alive and Terrifying Strike to control enemies.
advancement: Save coins to upgrade to Scale Mail (250) or Breastplate (750) and eventually Plate Harness (2,500), increase Fighting and Mysticism to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts and spells, raise Fortitude for survivability, consider Shield Mastery or more divine-focused talents.

name: Duelist
description: A swift, precise blade fighter who wins through footwork, feints, and pinpoint strikes.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Athletics, Stealth, Influence, Perception, Streetwise, Education

recommendedTalents.name: Defensive Dueling
recommendedTalents.gloss: +1 Parry while wielding a single non‑heavy melee weapon and no shield

recommendedTalents.name: Light Armor Mastery
recommendedTalents.gloss: In light armor, Evade once per scene without spending your Quick Action

recommendedTalents.name: Devious Tactics
recommendedTalents.gloss: Use Distract as a Quick Action, with anything nearby as the distraction

recommendedCombatArts.name: Quick Lunge
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Strike at their Dodge instead of Parry, and they get no reaction

recommendedCombatArts.name: Precise Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Ignore armor and add Agility to damage

playstyle: The Duelist is perfect for players who prefer agility and precision over brute force. Your shortsword is agile, so Agility carries both the attack and the damage, and every point of it works twice. Quick Lunge goes around a shield entirely by striking at Dodge, and it denies the reaction an armored opponent was counting on. Precise Strike ignores half their armor when the moment matters. Devious Tactics turns Distract into a Quick Action, and Light Armor Mastery gives you a free Evade each scene, so the one attack that gets through you meets Dodge 9 instead of Parry.
advancement: Increase Fighting and Athletics to rank 2-3, add Stealth or Influence depending on intrigue vs. street play, and consider Riposte to punish the attacks you make miss. A Twinblade is the agile upgrade worth saving for, but only once Dual Wielder is on your sheet.

name: Druid
description: A nature spellcaster who shapeshifts and commands elemental forces through communion with the natural world.
suggestedSkills: Mysticism, Nature, Survival, Lore, Insight, Perception, Athletics

recommendedTalents.name: Shape Changer
recommendedTalents.gloss: Transform into animal forms

recommendedTalents.name: Animal Companion
recommendedTalents.gloss: Control an animal companion (Tier ≤ Nature)

recommendedTalents.name: Explorer of Nature
recommendedTalents.gloss: Pick one environment: re-roll Survival and Nature there once per scene

recommendedCompanions.name: Bear
recommendedCompanions.gloss: Tough frontline with knockdown and grapple options and an intimidating roar.

recommendedCompanions.name: Bird
recommendedCompanions.gloss: Fast flying scout with keen eyes and dive attack bursts.

recommendedCompanions.name: Constrictor Snake
recommendedCompanions.gloss: Grapple and restrain to lock down priority targets.

playstyle: The Druid is perfect for players who want to blend with nature, shapeshift, and command elemental forces. Beast Form is where the build turns on: Shape Changer gives you 5 temporary HP on top of the spell and +2 damage with the natural weapons the form gives you, so shifting is a real combat option rather than a party trick. Bestial Adaptation is a Quick Action for the smaller changes, Lashing Vine costs no Focus and controls a space, and Lightning Javelin is your answer when something needs to die now. Animal Companion gives you a loyal ally, and Explorer of Nature makes your chosen country somewhere you are never lost or surprised.
advancement: Increase Mysticism to rank 2-3 for more powerful spells and Shape Changer options, raise Nature and Survival for wilderness mastery, add Lore for deeper nature knowledge, and consider more shapeshifting or elemental talents. Mesh of Vines is the area control you gave up at creation and is worth learning back early.

name: Engineer
description: A siege and devices specialist who improvises tools, sets traps, and supports allies with clever engineering and thrown contraptions.
suggestedSkills: Crafting, Education, Archery, Lore, Perception, Fortitude, Streetwise

recommendedTalents.name: Bomb Maker
recommendedTalents.gloss: Brew your own bombs in the field, up to Quality 2

recommendedTalents.name: Tactician
recommendedTalents.gloss: Scout a fight beforehand: the party re-rolls Initiative and opens with boons

recommendedTalents.name: Expert Slinger
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re-roll Supply checks for thrown weapons

recommendedCombatArts.name: Aimed Shot
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain +1 boon when not moving

recommendedCombatArts.name: Volley
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Hit multiple enemies with thrown weapons

startingEquipment.note: one use spent per bomb you build
replaces your standard pack: no load of its own, +2 carrying capacity

playstyle: The Engineer is perfect for players who enjoy battlefield problem‑solving and logistics. Bomb Maker turns an exploration turn and a use of materials into ordnance: thunderstones to deafen a room, smoke to break line of sight, fire bombs for a packed corridor. Every bomb is a thrown weapon, so your Archery delivers it, Aimed Shot makes the important throw land, and Volley scatters one across three enemies. Expert Slinger is what keeps you supplied, since every bundle you throw forces a Supply check after the fight. Tactician means the fight starts on your terms: scout it first and the party opens with boons.
advancement: Increase Crafting to rank 2-3 for higher-Quality bombs and a second build per rest, add Perception for scouting, and raise Archery for more Combat Arts and range. Efficient Worker keeps your materials from running dry, and Quick Construction is worth taking once your Strength can carry it.

name: Fighter
description: A frontline soldier who fights with a great blade, drawing every eye on the field and outlasting what comes back.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Athletics, Fortitude, Influence, Perception, Insight, Archery

recommendedTalents.name: Art of Fighting
recommendedTalents.gloss: Learn two more melee Combat Arts, no action needed

recommendedTalents.name: Bulky
recommendedTalents.gloss: +2 HP and +2 carrying capacity, with no action to spend

recommendedTalents.name: Second Wind
recommendedTalents.gloss: Regain HP with Quick Action once per scene

recommendedCombatArts.name: Defensive Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain Defend Action effects on hit

recommendedCombatArts.name: Charge
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Move and shove while attacking

recommendedCombatArts.name: Cleave
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Hit up to two extra creatures in your weapon's reach

recommendedCombatArts.name: Divert Attention
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Your attack also distracts the target onto you

recommendedCombatArts.name: Aimed Shot
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain +1 boon on a thrown attack when you don't move

startingEquipment.note: thrown opener for the Archery rank 0 art

playstyle: The Fighter is perfect for players who want straightforward, effective combat with tactical depth. A greatsword deals 4 weapon damage and reaches two extra enemies with Cleave, so a knot of foes is where you want to stand. You have no shield, so you hold the line by being the one worth hitting: Divert Attention turns an attack into a Distract, and Protect Ally still lets you step in front of a blow and take it on Parry 9. Bulky asks for no action at all and leaves you with 24 HP, the most in the set, and Second Wind gives 4 of them back once a scene. Art of Fighting is why you have five Combat Arts instead of three, which is the real difference between a Fighter and everyone else who swings a sword. The javelin plus Aimed Shot answers the enemy you cannot reach.
advancement: Increase Fighting and Fortitude to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts and resilience, add Athletics for mobility under a heavy weapon, and consider Heavy Weapon Mastery or Blade Mastery to widen what the greatsword can answer.

name: Gladiator
description: An arena fighter who fights with chain and net, tangling opponents at reach and putting them in the sand where the crowd can see it.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Athletics, Influence, Fortitude, Perception, Streetwise, Stealth

recommendedTalents.name: Disciplined Fighter
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re-roll one melee attack per scene, for the throw that has to land

recommendedTalents.name: Grappler
recommendedTalents.gloss: Every chain hit can become a grapple

recommendedTalents.name: Leading Presence
recommendedTalents.gloss: Allies near you gain boons to Initiative and vs fear

recommendedCombatArts.name: Snare
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Grapple them and they are restrained, prone on a strong hit

recommendedCombatArts.name: Felling Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: The attack counts as a Trip: they go down and stay down

startingEquipment.note: the net of the sand, though you throw it untrained

playstyle: The Gladiator is perfect for players who want to control a fight rather than end it quickly. The spiked chain has reach, so you strike from close range and they have to come to you. Grappler turns any hit into a grapple, which is what Snare hangs off: restrained, and prone on a strong hit. Felling Strike puts them in the sand without a grapple at all. You will not out-damage a greataxe and you are not trying to: the enemy you have tangled is the one your party kills. Leading Presence works the crowd and the line at the same time.
advancement: Increase Fighting to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts, raise Athletics to hold your grapples against stronger foes, and add Fortitude for resilience. Choking Grip is the next art worth having, and Banded Leather is the first purchase your spare coins should go to.

name: Hoplite
description: A formation fighter with spear and shield, representing the Bronze Age soldier's tactical prowess.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Athletics, Influence, Fortitude, Perception, Insight, Archery

recommendedTalents.name: Polearm Mastery
recommendedTalents.gloss: Opportunity attacks when enemies approach

recommendedTalents.name: Bull Rush
recommendedTalents.gloss: Boons on Shove and Trip, and your pushes send them a short distance

recommendedTalents.name: Leading Presence
recommendedTalents.gloss: Allies near you gain boons to Initiative and vs fear

recommendedCombatArts.name: Charge
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Move and shove while attacking

recommendedCombatArts.name: Defensive Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain Defend Action effects on hit

recommendedCombatArts.name: Pinning Shot
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: A hit with a thrown javelin drops the target’s Movement to 0

playstyle: The Hoplite is perfect for players who enjoy tactical positioning, defensive play, and Bronze Age military aesthetics. Your spear has reach, so your place is one step back: you strike at close range, and you suffer +1 bane on the attack whenever an enemy is right on top of you. Everything else follows from that. Polearm Mastery punishes anyone who walks into your reach, Bull Rush shoves them back out to where your spear wants them, and Charge counts as a Shove so it benefits too. Leading Presence coordinates your unit, Defensive Strike holds the line, and the javelin with Pinning Shot stops the enemy who thought they could run past you.
advancement: Increase Fighting to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts, raise Athletics and Influence for tactical command, add Fortitude for resilience, consider Shield Mastery or Protective Stance, and save for heavier armor (Scale Mail 250 coins). Your spear is versatile, so dropping the shield for both hands is +1 weapon damage whenever you would rather kill than hold.

name: Magus
description: A melee fighter who infuses weapons with arcane magic, blending swordplay and spellcasting.
suggestedSkills: Arcana, Fighting, Education, Lore, Perception, Insight, Streetwise

recommendedTalents.name: Spellblade
recommendedTalents.gloss: Quick Action and 2 Focus: a rank 0 spell rides your weapon attack

recommendedTalents.name: Blade Mastery
recommendedTalents.gloss: Switch between pierce/slash properties

recommendedTalents.name: Eloquent Talker
recommendedTalents.gloss: Argue with Education in place of Influence, on your best die

recommendedCombatArts.name: Quick Lunge
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Strike at their Dodge instead of Parry, and they get no reaction

recommendedCombatArts.name: Deep Cut
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Flip your blade to slash with Blade Mastery, then leave them bleeding

playstyle: The Magus is perfect for players who want to combine melee combat with spellcasting in a hybrid warrior-mage. Spellblade is the archetype in one line: spend your Quick Action and 2 extra Focus, and a rank 0 spell rides your longsword instead of being cast at range. Both of your disciplines carry two rank 0 spells that qualify, and Focus 8 pays for it three times a scene. Your two arts split the enemy roster and Blade Mastery is the switch between them: against armor, Quick Lunge strikes at their Dodge and denies them a reaction; against light or no armor, flip the longsword to slash and Deep Cut leaves them bleeding. Eloquent Talker means the scholar half of you talks with Mind and Education instead of the Spirit you do not have.
advancement: Increase Arcana and Fighting equally to rank 2-3 for more spells and Combat Arts, and take Battle Mage next: at AV 2 with Dodge 7, a Quick Action barrier for 2 Focus is the defence you gave up to get Spellblade at creation. Add Lore for magical knowledge, and Mana Shield once you cast rank 1 spells often.

name: Monk
description: An unarmed combat specialist with superhuman toughness and grappling techniques.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Athletics, Fortitude, Insight, Perception, Mysticism, Education

recommendedTalents.name: Pugilist
recommendedTalents.gloss: Fists and simple weapons both count as brawling weapons, +1 Parry

recommendedTalents.name: Grappler
recommendedTalents.gloss: Grapple on hit with unarmed/brawling weapons

recommendedTalents.name: Body of Bronze
recommendedTalents.gloss: +2 HP, +1+Fortitude AV while unarmored

recommendedCombatArts.name: Choking Grip
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Restrain grappled targets

recommendedCombatArts.name: Knockout
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Stun enemies with crush attacks

startingEquipment.note: simple, so it counts as a brawling weapon for you
the one piece of armor Body of Bronze still allows

playstyle: The Monk is perfect for players who want to fight without weapons or armor, using martial arts and grappling. Pugilist makes your fists count as brawling weapons, and it does the same for simple weapons, so your quarterstaff is part of the style rather than a compromise: +1 Parry either way, and Grappler and both your Combat Arts work with staff or empty hands. Body of Bronze gives you 1 + Fortitude as armor while you wear none, and a helmet is still allowed, so you stand at AV 3 with nothing on your body. Grappler turns any hit into a grapple, which is what Choking Grip hangs off, and Knockout can put a heavily armored enemy on the floor entirely.
advancement: Increase Fighting and Athletics to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts and grappling options, raise Fortitude for more toughness, add Insight for reading opponents, and take Martial Artist next: it makes your unarmed attacks and your staff count as agile, which moves your whole style onto Agility if you would rather be quick than strong.

name: Oracle
description: A divine prophet who uses foresight and omens to guide allies and reveal hidden truths.
suggestedSkills: Mysticism, Lore, Insight, Education, Perception, Influence, Stealth

recommendedTalents.name: Divine Favor
recommendedTalents.gloss: Pray at rest for Favor, then spend it to bless an ally‘s roll

recommendedTalents.name: Consult the Myths
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re‑roll Lore about supernatural topics once per scene

recommendedTalents.name: Take Their Measure
recommendedTalents.gloss: Study a creature and the GM tells you their next move, fear, or weak point

playstyle: The Oracle is perfect for players who enjoy support roles, being the party's guide, and themes of fate and prophecy. Between scenes you are the party's compass: Thread of Fate names which of two courses holds the better fortune, and Take Their Measure has the GM tell you what a creature will do next, what it fears, or where it is weakest. In a fight you are not helpless. Stern Gaze costs no Focus and hits their Resist, and it deals more and dazes them once your Light magic has already blinded or unmasked them. Moment of Clarity is a Quick Action that lets an ally throw off a charm or a fright, and Curse of Twilight leaves an enemy half blind and slow to act. Divine Favor is the blessing itself: pray at rest, then spend Favor with no action at all to put a boon on an ally's roll at the moment it matters.
advancement: Increase Mysticism and Lore to rank 2-3 for more powerful spells and deeper knowledge, raise Insight for better intuition, learn more divination and revelation spells, add Education for broader knowledge, and take Divine Rites so you can pray your Focus back during a break. Detect Lies and Blessing of Light are the revelations you skipped at creation and are worth picking up early.

name: Priest
description: A divine healer who mends wounds, shields the failing, and calls calm down onto a fight before it turns.
suggestedSkills: Mysticism, Fighting, Lore, Influence, Insight, Fortitude, Education

recommendedTalents.name: Armor of the Faithful
recommendedTalents.gloss: Wear no armor and faith is your armor: 1 + Mysticism as AV

recommendedTalents.name: Consult the Myths
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re‑roll Lore about supernatural topics once per scene

recommendedTalents.name: Rallying Cry
recommendedTalents.gloss: Quick Action: an ally shakes off fright or a daze, or gains a boon

recommendedCombatArts.name: Exhilarating Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: A hit heals you and every ally close to you

startingEquipment.note: for the wound your spells cannot close

playstyle: The Priest is perfect for players who want to support allies with healing and protection while remaining combat-effective. You wear no armor on purpose: Armor of the Faithful gives you 1 + Mysticism as your armor, and a shield still counts as wearing none, so you stand at AV 3 in a robe. As your Mysticism grows, so does your skin. You are the party's healer first and everything else second, and the only Devotion of Life in the set: nobody mends a wound like you do. Your mace and shield exist so that standing near the fighting is survivable, since your healing reaches only as far as your hand does, and the mace is crush, so it ignores half of whatever armor your enemies wear. Rallying Cry pulls an ally out of a fright or a daze for a Quick Action, and Exhilarating Strike is the one attack worth making: a hit heals you and every ally close to you. Defensive Strike keeps you standing, and Exhilarating Strike heals you and every ally near you on a hit, which is the closest thing in the game to fighting and healing in the same breath.
advancement: Increase Mysticism to rank 2-3 for more powerful spells, raise Influence for stronger authority and rallying, take Fighting to rank 1 if you want a second Combat Art and a steadier Parry, and learn Rapid Vitality or Sustaining Grace when you tire of spending your whole Action to heal: both are Quick Actions, where Healing Touch is slow but heals far more. Divine Rites is worth taking once your spells cost more Focus than a fight can spare.

name: Ranger
description: A ranged hunter with wilderness expertise who strikes from distance with precision while tracking prey.
suggestedSkills: Archery, Survival, Nature, Insight, Perception, Stealth, Fighting

recommendedTalents.name: Sharpshooter
recommendedTalents.gloss: Ignore the first bane from attacking beyond normal range

recommendedTalents.name: Monster Hunter
recommendedTalents.gloss: Quick Action: mark a creature bigger than you and deal +2 damage to it

recommendedTalents.name: Animal Companion
recommendedTalents.gloss: Control an animal companion (Tier ≤ Nature)

recommendedCombatArts.name: Aimed Shot
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain +1 boon when not moving

recommendedCombatArts.name: Precise Shot
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Ignore armor and add Agility to damage

recommendedCombatArts.name: Evasive Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: A melee hit grants the Retreat Action, breaking back to range

recommendedCompanions.name: Dog
recommendedCompanions.gloss: Loyal tracker with pack tactics and reliable grapples.

recommendedCompanions.name: Bird
recommendedCompanions.gloss: Fast flying scout with keen eyes and dive attack bursts.

recommendedCompanions.name: Bear
recommendedCompanions.gloss: Tough frontline with knockdown and grapple options and an intimidating roar.

playstyle: The Ranger is perfect for players who enjoy ranged combat, wilderness survival, and having an animal companion. Strike from distance with precision while your animal companion provides tactical support. Your longbow hits for 8, 12 or 16 and Sharpshooter carries it out past its normal range, so pick your ground and make them cross it. Against anything bigger than you, spend a Quick Action on Monster Hunter first: +2 damage for a short duration, which is the difference between wounding a beast and dropping it. Aimed Shot rewards holding still, Precise Shot cuts through armor, and Evasive Strike is there for the moment something reaches you: hit it, then break back to range.
advancement: Increase Archery to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts and damage, raise Survival and Nature for wilderness mastery, add Perception for better awareness, and consider Disciplined Archer or Reflexive Shooter, which keeps your bow working when enemies close. Relentless Tracker is worth picking up once Survival reaches rank 2 if tracking is your table's currency. Rapid Shot needs a non-heavy bow, so it does nothing for a longbow.

name: Rogue
description: A sneaky infiltrator who uses tricks, stealth, and precision strikes to eliminate targets.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Stealth, Streetwise, Insight, Perception, Athletics, Influence

recommendedTalents.name: Disciplined Fighter
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re-roll one melee attack per scene, for the strike that only comes once

recommendedTalents.name: Assassination
recommendedTalents.gloss: Your first hit each scene on an enemy unaware of you deals +2 damage

recommendedTalents.name: Jack of All Trades
recommendedTalents.gloss: Add Streetwise to any one roll once per scene

recommendedCombatArts.name: Feint
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain +1 boon when not moving with non-heavy weapons

recommendedCombatArts.name: Evasive Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain Retreat Action effects on hit

startingEquipment.note: locks, traps, and the doors nobody opened for you
replaces your standard pack: no load of its own, +2 carrying capacity

playstyle: The Rogue is perfect for players who enjoy stealth, infiltration, skill-based challenges, and being the party's scout. Everything you do is built around one strike. Set up unseen, hold still so Feint gives you +1 boon, and open with Assassination for +2 damage on an enemy who has no idea you are there, with poison on the blade for another +2 that ignores armor entirely. Disciplined Fighter re-rolls that attack if it misses, because it only comes once a scene. Then Evasive Strike lets you hit and break away without an opportunity attack, back to somewhere they have to find you again. Out of a fight, Thieves' Tools and Jack of All Trades mean there are very few doors, locks or conversations you have no answer for.
advancement: Increase Stealth and Fighting to rank 2-3 for more options and Combat Arts, add Insight for reading people, and take Infiltrator to make locks and traps your specialty or Shadow Slip to slide out of the one attack that finds you. Blade Mastery is worth revisiting once you learn Deep Cut, which it turns on.

name: Shaman
description: A spirit medium who communes with ancestors to bless allies and curse enemies through spiritual power.
suggestedSkills: Mysticism, Nature, Lore, Insight, Survival, Perception, Influence

recommendedTalents.name: Divine Sense
recommendedTalents.gloss: Sense spirits/undead and hallowed or cursed auras

recommendedTalents.name: Herbalist
recommendedTalents.gloss: Brew remedies in the field, up to Quality 2

recommendedTalents.name: Consult the Myths
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re‑roll Lore about supernatural topics once per scene

playstyle: The Shaman is perfect for players who enjoy spiritual themes, supporting through blessings, and connecting with ancestral powers. Bridge the physical and spirit worlds. Commune with Ancestors is what the archetype is named for: pour a libation, name your honored dead, and describe the problem that weighs on you, and the spirits answer. In a fight your magic costs nothing to start: Minor Hex hangs a small doom on an enemy so their next roll suffers a bane, and Spared from Death lets you reach across a room to a dying ally and add to the roll that decides whether they live. Healing Touch is the one spell you spend Focus on, and it mends what a salve cannot. Divine Sense finds the spirits and undead nobody else can see, and Herbalist keeps your people supplied with remedies between the fights.
advancement: Increase Mysticism to rank 2-3 for more powerful spells, raise Lore for deeper spiritual knowledge, add Insight for reading people and spirits, and learn Curse of Death and Glimpse of Mortality as your curses deepen. Field Medic is worth taking at Nature rank 2 if your party has no other healer.

name: Slinger
description: A mobile short-range skirmisher who uses slings and thrown weapons for hit-and-run tactics.
suggestedSkills: Archery, Athletics, Stealth, Survival, Perception, Insight, Nature

recommendedTalents.name: Ammo Specialist
recommendedTalents.gloss: Supply checks for your ammo: roll twice, take the higher

recommendedTalents.name: Fast Stride
recommendedTalents.gloss: Use Dash as Quick Action

recommendedTalents.name: Leading the Way
recommendedTalents.gloss: Your sneaking carries the whole party, not just you

recommendedCombatArts.name: Pinning Shot
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Their Movement drops to 0, or they are restrained on a strong hit

recommendedCombatArts.name: Disabling Shot
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Your sling is crush, so a hit can leave them dazed

startingEquipment.note: entangles anything up to large, for the one that closes on you
replaces your standard pack: no load of its own, +2 carrying capacity

playstyle: The Slinger is perfect for players who want a mobile, hit-and-run playstyle with simple but effective ranged combat. Harass from short range, then reposition with Fast Stride. Your arts exist to keep the distance you just made: Pinning Shot drops their Movement to zero, and Disabling Shot works because a sling is crush, leaving them dazed instead of chasing you. The bola is the answer to whoever closes anyway: it entangles anything up to large size, and your Strength meets its requirement exactly. Ammo Specialist keeps your stones from running out, and Leading the Way means the whole party moves unseen when you scout ahead, not just you. Watch your load. At 11 you are exactly at capacity, and going over would cost you the Dash Action that Fast Stride is for.
advancement: Increase Archery to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts and damage, raise Athletics for mobility, add Survival for scouting, and consider Rapid Shot, which works because a sling is not heavy. Snare is worth learning once you carry the bola: an entangling throw counts as a grapple, which is what that art hangs off. Keep coins spare, since every bundle you throw depletes.

name: Sorcerer
description: A glass cannon spellcaster who deals massive magical damage through raw arcane power.
suggestedSkills: Arcana, Lore, Education, Insight, Perception, Stealth, Influence

recommendedTalents.name: Inexhaustible Mind
recommendedTalents.gloss: Meditate on a short break to get half your Focus back

recommendedTalents.name: Magical Sense
recommendedTalents.gloss: Gain boons against magic. Intuit resistances and weaknesses

recommendedTalents.name: General Education
recommendedTalents.gloss: No bane on untrained expert skills with Mind

startingEquipment.note: 8 HP back, for the hit a 16 HP caster cannot take twice

playstyle: The Sorcerer is perfect for players who want to deal massive magical damage and control the battlefield through spells. Unleash raw arcane power. Flickering Flame and Frost Snap cost no Focus at all, so your ordinary turn is 6 to 10 damage for free, and Chromatic Orb is what you spend Focus on: it picks its damage type as you cast, so nothing resists you twice. Elemental Ward is your only defence in the moment, a Quick Action reaction that adds +2 to the Defense being attacked, and Inexhaustible Mind means a short break puts half your Focus back and the artillery keeps firing. You have 16 HP and AV 2. Stand behind someone.
advancement: Increase Arcana to rank 2-3 for more powerful spells and additional spells known, add Insight for better awareness, and consider Spellweaver for Metamagic or Mana Shield once your spells are rank 2 and the barrier it grants is worth having. Adopting a second discipline widens what you can answer, at the cost of depth in Evocation.

name: Swashbuckler
description: A street-born duelist who fights dirty with feints, distractions, and flashy blade work. Excels with light weapons, mobility, and crowd-savvy tricks.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Stealth, Streetwise, Insight, Perception, Athletics, Influence

recommendedTalents.name: Dual Wielder
recommendedTalents.gloss: No banes when attacking with two light melee weapons

recommendedTalents.name: Light Armor Mastery
recommendedTalents.gloss: In light armor, Evade once per scene without spending your Quick Action

recommendedTalents.name: Swashbuckler
recommendedTalents.gloss: +2 HP, on a hit with a light melee weapon, target can’t use Quick Actions against you this turn

recommendedCombatArts.name: Quick Lunge
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Strike at their Dodge, and they get no reaction to it

recommendedCombatArts.name: Disarm
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Attempt to disarm immediately after this attack

playstyle: The Swashbuckler thrives on movement and momentum. Dual Wielder means both blades swing in one Action with no banes, and every hit is 6 to 10 damage plus 2 more from the poison you coated them with. Your whole game is denying answers: the Swashbuckler talent stops an enemy you hit from using Quick Actions against you for the turn, and Quick Lunge denies the reaction to the attack itself while striking at their Dodge instead of their Parry. Disarm takes the weapon out of their hand entirely. Light Armor Mastery gives you a free Evade each scene, so the one attack that finds you meets Dodge 9.
advancement: Raise Fighting to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts (Supreme Feint, Quick Lunge, or Riposte). Boost Athletics for mobility or Streetwise for Thug Tactics if you prefer gang-up brawling. Stealth is worth adding if you want the ambush half of the street as well as the duel. Consider Defensive Dueling if you pivot to single-blade finesse. Add Fortitude for toughness and Influence for swagger-driven social play.

name: Summoner
description: An arcane conjurer who brings allies from beyond and shapes the field with glyphs and constructs.
suggestedSkills: Arcana, Lore, Insight, Education, Perception, Influence, Streetwise

recommendedTalents.name: Master of Fundamentals
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re‑roll one arcane rank 0 spell per scene

recommendedTalents.name: Magical Sense
recommendedTalents.gloss: Boons vs. magic. Intuit resistances and weaknesses

recommendedTalents.name: Piercing Look
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re‑roll Insight vs. lies/motives once per scene

recommendedFamiliars.name: Bat
recommendedFamiliars.gloss: Flying scout with echolocation and a poisoning bite.

recommendedFamiliars.name: Rat
recommendedFamiliars.gloss: Climbing scout with keen scent and a bleeding bite.

recommendedFamiliars.name: Spider
recommendedFamiliars.gloss: Web control once per scene for restraint.

playstyle: The Summoner controls tempo with glyphs and durable constructs while adding bodies to the field. Arcane Bolt costs no Focus and dazes on a strong hit, so you always have a turn. Arcane Glyph is a trap you lay before the fight, and Arcane Barrier is a door of force you drop into a corridor mid-fight to decide who reaches whom. Master of Fundamentals re-rolls one of your free spells each scene. Conjure Familiar is a ritual of hours costing 100 coins of incense, which your starting purse covers, so you can begin play with your familiar already beside you. Later, Summon Aberration adds real battlefield presence.
advancement: Raise Arcana 2-3 for more spells and Focus. Consider Inexhaustible Mind or Spellweaver. Add Education for arcane theory and Streetwise for the places a familiar can scout but you cannot walk. After your familiar, look to Summon Aberration and utility control like Arcane Eye.

name: Tamer
description: A non-magical animal handler who commands a loyal companion and controls space with a whip and clever tactics.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Nature, Athletics, Survival, Perception, Insight, Streetwise

recommendedTalents.name: Riposte
recommendedTalents.gloss: Miss you in melee and your whip answers with a free attack

recommendedTalents.name: Animal Companion
recommendedTalents.gloss: Control an animal companion (Tier ≤ Nature)

recommendedTalents.name: Grappler
recommendedTalents.gloss: Any whip hit can also grapple them, which is what Snare needs

recommendedCombatArts.name: Disarm
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Attempt to disarm immediately after this attack

recommendedCombatArts.name: Snare
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Grapple and restrain with your weapon on a hit

startingEquipment.note: replaces your standard pack: no load of its own, +2 carrying capacity

recommendedCompanions.name: Dog
recommendedCompanions.gloss: Loyal tracker with pack tactics and reliable grapples.

recommendedCompanions.name: Cat
recommendedCompanions.gloss: Stealthy scout with pounce and knockdown.

recommendedCompanions.name: Boar
recommendedCompanions.gloss: Durable frontline that can gore on a charge.

playstyle: The Tamer locks lanes and creates openings for their animal. Your whip has reach, so you fight from close range and Riposte punishes anyone who swings at you and misses. Grappler turns any whip hit into a grapple, which is what Snare hangs off: restrained, and prone on a strong hit, with your companion already on top of them. Disarm strips the threat out of their hands entirely. Your companion is your second body. Set up flanks and force bad choices.
advancement: Raise Nature 2-3 to deepen companion options. Fighting 2-3 for more Combat Arts (Supreme Disarm, Flurry). Add Survival for fieldcraft and Fast Stride from Athletics if you would rather kite than hold a lane. Consider Field Medic from Nature for downtime care.

name: Warlock
description: An eldritch spellcaster who wields dark pact magic to curse enemies and drain their life force.
suggestedSkills: Arcana, Lore, Insight, Influence, Perception, Stealth, Fortitude

recommendedTalents.name: Wild Overload
recommendedTalents.gloss: Overload a rank 1 spell for a surge of unstable power

recommendedTalents.name: Mage Hunter
recommendedTalents.gloss: Enemies suffer +1 bane on Spell Concentration from your damage

recommendedTalents.name: Read the Room
recommendedTalents.gloss: Study an NPC to learn one of their Motivations

playstyle: The Warlock is perfect for players who enjoy morally complex characters with manipulative magic and dark themes. Your power is borrowed, not earned, and it strains against you. Wild Overload lets you push a rank 1 spell past its safe limits when a fight needs to end now, at the risk of a wild surge. Mage Hunter turns your own damage into a weapon against enemy spellcasters, because every point you deal makes their concentration harder to hold. Out of combat, Read the Room hands you what a person wants or fears, which is where mind control actually starts.
advancement: Increase Arcana to rank 2-3 for more powerful spells and additional spells known, raise Lore for deeper occult knowledge, add Fortitude to survive your own backlash, and consider Spellweaver for Metamagic Arts.

name: Warlord
description: A battlefield leader who commands allies from the second rank, striking past the front line with a glaive while directing the fight.
suggestedSkills: Fighting, Influence, Education, Fortitude, Insight, Perception, Athletics

recommendedTalents.name: Disciplined Fighter
recommendedTalents.gloss: Re-roll any melee attack once per scene

recommendedTalents.name: Leading Presence
recommendedTalents.gloss: Allies near you gain boons to Initiative and vs fear

recommendedTalents.name: Commander
recommendedTalents.gloss: Grant allies movement or boons as Quick Action

recommendedCombatArts.name: Exhilarating Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Heal nearby allies on hit

recommendedCombatArts.name: Defensive Strike
recommendedCombatArts.gloss: Gain Defend Action effects on hit

playstyle: The Warlord is perfect for players who want to lead the party tactically, enhancing allies rather than focusing on personal combat. The glaive has reach, so you strike over the front rank without standing in it, which is what keeps your Quick Action free for Commander every single round. Commander is the whole build: an ally gets +1 Movement or +1 boon on their next roll, on their turn, from you. Leading Presence costs nothing and hands the whole party boons on Initiative and against fear. Disciplined Fighter is your one free re-roll on a melee attack, so it never competes with commanding. Use Exhilarating Strike to heal allies on a hit and Defensive Strike when something reaches you anyway.
advancement: Increase Fighting and Influence to rank 2-3 for more Combat Arts and leadership abilities, raise Education for tactical options, add Fortitude for survivability, and consider Polearm Mastery to make the reach work harder.
